body: **2026-11-17-standing-live-rig** (11. A11y Anti-Patterns, 1 row) — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing` gained its except: the test-only standing live rig may read the trust selector's place, the input box as empty, holds-text or absent, and modal dialogs, as closed words only, its raw frames kept local and gitignored. The v2-33 live starts on the rig rest on this exception. Showing that no trust dialog rose must use the same closed words and must not stretch the exception into the product. The rig's own trust pass (`crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/isolate.rs`) must not hide the product's mechanism.

**2026-11-13-verify-readiness-on-the-input-box** (11. A11y Anti-Patterns, 1 row) — `~ decision/no-screen-content-parsing` limited parsing of the vendor screen to compiled signatures (footer literals, the input box's rule and prompt rows, modal literals), reading only the prompt row's opening char, as a ratified boundary widening. If the product has to detect "opened at its input box with no trust dialog", it must use the existing signatures. Adding a trust-dialog signature to the product would widen this row again and needs the founder's word.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** — Made `contract/tui-passthrough/entry` and `contract/tui-passthrough/own-bytes`: the passthrough is entered by `viola run` and by a passed `viola revive`, and a revived start writes no line of its own while the child holds the terminal (`tests/chaos_revive.rs`). The no-conformance-claim ban and the keystroke ban also cover a revive start. If revive's start arm shares the trust mechanism (the snapshot's `cwd`), the same boundary clauses bind it.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — Precedent: a start variant that wrote a config override before the spawn and passed a flag (`--settings`) got its own reading of the zero-viola-bytes clause, `passthrough_with_a_statusline_source_adds_no_viola_bytes` in `tests/tui_passthrough.rs`. A start that now writes trust state, or passes a trust flag, is a new start variant. By this precedent it owes a zero-viola-bytes reading of its own (`contract/tui-passthrough/viola-terminal-bytes`, `decision/zero-viola-bytes-on-the-terminal`).

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — Removed the statusline arm and its passthrough case (`− decision/statusline-output-passed-byte-for-byte`), dropped the 5 s statusline deadline from `decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` and `decision/time-bounds-never-on-human`, and retired `contract/viola-hook-statusline/exit`. As a result viola now writes no `--settings` override, which matches the scope's standing ban on `--settings` and `settings.json`. Any wait the trust mechanism adds must join these time-bound rows and fall on viola's child, never on the human.

**2026-11-14-budget-gate-removed** — Dropped the budget pause from `decision/time-bounds-fall-on-the-driver` and `decision/time-bounds-never-on-human`, and retired exit 11 (`contract/cli-exit-codes/11`, never reused). This is the current list of time bounds and the current exit map. A new start refusal cannot take 11.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** — Several entries matter here. (a) The tui is hosted on openpty alone. The zero-viola-bytes case compares the outer-PTY stream byte for byte with an unwrapped fake-agent run, and each boundary clause is a nextest case on `ubuntu-latest`, so a v2-33 e2e on the fake agent can follow this comparison. (b) The Linux-only platform line (`decision/linux-only`). (c) The cli and tui cases run in the single `coverage` suite on `ubuntu-latest` (`decision/cli-invariants-pass-in-ci`). (d) revive's `--json` start codes are ten, without `batch-script-child`. (e) The frame verbs' strict-modes refusals leave the mode as found, with the Windows ACL and NotFound arms retired.

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** — Several entries matter here. (a) `viola revive --json` prints one exit-1 document for every refusal of the start it shares with `run` (`contract/viola-revive-json/start-refusal`, `contract/start-json-refusal/document`). A `claude` not found reads as `internal-error`, and a `pump_child` error prints no document. (b) Under `--json`, the `cli` catch site prints the `internal-error` document (`contract/json-fault/internal-error`), while run and revive's start stay silent. (c) A stale holder reads `stale-heartbeat` (`contract/revive-json-refusal/stale-heartbeat`). (d) One hint per code and no hint names release (`decision/one-hint-per-code`, `decision/no-hint-names-release`, `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs`). If a failed trust write or flag refuses the start, it must fit this catalogue: a new closed word is the founder's to give, as these were.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (a refused socket directory at the start) — Precedent for adding a check to the shared run/revive start before the child spawns. It refuses with exit 1 before any snapshot, bind or child, prints the fixed `unable:`/`hint:` pair naming only the parsed name with no path, and gives revive's `--json` one new code (`socket-dir-refused`, the founder's own word). It leaves the directory as found (`contract/start-refusal/socket-dir`, `decision/socket-dir-refusal-before-any-frame`, `contract/cli-fixed-message/form`). A refusal arm for the trust write (an absent, unreadable, link or non-JSON `~/.claude.json`) would follow the same shape and need the founder's word.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the strict-modes refusals at run, revive start and verify) — `viola run`, a revive start and `viola verify` refuse a home tree that fails the strict-modes check before any log opens: exit 1, the home-state pair with `hint:` last, and no child (`contract/start-refusal/home-strict-modes`, `decision/strict-modes-refusal-before-any-write`). This fixes where the start's checks come in order. A trust write placed before the spawn must sit after these refusals and write nothing when they refuse.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — Several entries matter here. (a) Each `--json` failure is one document with a literal exit, empty stderr, no ESC byte and a body holding no path or upstream text (`decision/json-failure-documents-are-clean`, `contract/cli-json-failure/document`). (b) The exit-2 exception: `viola answer` and `viola send` print a fixed stderr line and no document (`decision/json-one-document-no-hint`). (c) A code word outside the closed list stays visible and takes exit 14 (`decision/unlisted-code-words-stay-visible`, `contract/code-word/format`). (d) A fault reads `wrapper fault` and carries no hint (`contract/human-fault-line/wrapper-fault`). (e) The census of error writers (`decision/error-bodies-have-writer-and-witness`, `decision/thiserror-messages-interpolate-nothing`). Any new error writer for the trust write must be named in the census and must carry no `~/.claude.json` path or content, in line with the scope's "nothing of the CLI's config file logged".

**2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract** — Gave revive `--json` on both arms: each exit-1 refusal is `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` on stdout with empty stderr, and the human `unable:`/`hint:` pair stays byte-identical (`contract/revive-json-refusal/document`, `contract/revive-human-refusal/pair`). This is the base form a trust-related start refusal would take.

**2026-10-08-first-live-test-and-self-drive** — First live reading of the takeover clause, recorded as supplemental and never gating (`decision/live-readings-never-gate`). The live starts on the standing rig that prove v2-33 are supplemental readings of the same kind. The gating proof must be the e2e on the fake agent.

**2026-10-19-overseer-switch-to-viola** — Second live reading of the takeover clause, on the product binary over a real `claude`, again supplemental and never gating. This is precedent for recording live readings on a real CLI version in the keyboard-test-harness key without making them a gate.

**2026-10-04-the-wheel** — Fixed the closed non-editing set (focus, mouse and terminal replies) and the boundary case in which focus, mouse and resize never move the wheel (`decision/wheel-ignores-terminal-events`, `contract/tui-passthrough/human-keystrokes`). The chunk's boundary is that viola types no key into the trust dialog. Any byte viola sends to the child at start, if one were ever needed, would fall outside this set and break the rule that viola originates no keys.

**2026-11-06-version-done-check** — Several entries matter here. (a) The cli checks run on `std::process::Command` with literal pins (`decision/cli-a11y-by-literal-tests`, `decision/fixed-cli-strings-pinned-by-literal`, `decision/refusal-layout-literal-pins`). (b) The outer-PTY driver is portable-pty `=0.9.0`, which a11y never re-pins (`decision/tui-boundary-driver-pin`, `decision/portable-pty-outer-pty-driver`). Any new fixed refusal or hint string from the trust work must be pinned by literal.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — Built the colour decision (`NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, stdout's terminal state), with no SGR under `--json` or a passthrough role (`decision/colour-decision-inputs`, `decision/no-sgr-off-terminal`, `decision/sgr-beside-its-word`). Under `viola run` or a passed revive, nothing of viola's own, including anything from the trust step, may reach the terminal.

**2026-10-13-interrupted-verify-cleanup** — Added verify's interrupted pair (`contract/interrupted-verify/stderr`, `contract/viola-verify/interrupted-pair`). The scope keeps `viola verify`'s runs as they are unless P3 measures that the mechanism must reach them. A ledger-row probe for the relied trust behaviour adds a verify step line (`contract/viola-verify/step-line`) and must keep this pair intact.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** (the tui passthrough boundary after a contained vt100 feed panic) — The passthrough boundary holds after a feed panic: no viola literal reaches the outer terminal and the child's own bytes do. This is the existing reading of `contract/tui-passthrough/vendor-content` that a start variant must not weaken.

**2026-10-16-remove-the-browser-leg** — The cli and tui boundary cases are nextest cases in the `coverage` suite, with no a11y driver, stage or `suite` value of their own (`decision/no-a11y-tool-output-discipline-assertions`, `decision/output-discipline-a11y-fallback`). The v2-33 boundary case must be an ordinary nextest case there.

**2026-09-28-mutation-testing-to-the-epoch-boundary** — The CLI output-discipline invariants (P4, P6) meet mutation only at the epoch-boundary audit (`decision/cli-invariants-pass-in-ci`). This matches the directive's "no mutation run" for this chunk. Each acceptance predicate must still be able to fail when its guard is removed.

A session viola starts with viola run in a folder the installed claude CLI never trusted opens at its input box with no trust dialog shown and no key typed by viola, by the CLI's own trust mechanism (a trust flag or setting if P3 measures one, else a write of that folder's trust record into the user's claude config), never by emulating the human's key presses.
The user's own trust of every other folder stays unchanged; viola touches no other project's trust state, and nothing of the CLI's config file is logged.
The fake agent raises its trust dialog in an untrusted folder and honours the chosen mechanism, so the e2e acceptance (matrix v2-33) fails when the mechanism is gone; the run start path, and revive's start arm if it shares it, carries the mechanism before the child spawn.
P3 first re-measures the installed CLI's flags, settings and bundle strings for a trust mechanism, which config file the wrapped child reads, and re-verifies the carried claim that a trust record raised no dialog and took no key on claude 2.1.325.
The live starts on the standing rig are counted per CLI version with every byte the rig types, and the rig's own trust pass must not mask the product's.

body_fields.what: the test-only standing rig's isolation of a live start — its private claude config and the trust pass it writes there under the founder's grant — edits: the rig's trust pass

body: The viola run TUI passthrough at a start: viola writes zero bytes of its own to the terminal and types no key into the child, so the CLI-native trust dialog is never answered by viola; the session reaches the input box with the terminal belonging to the child.
Human keystrokes at a start stay the human's: viola never blocks or emulates them, and no trust-dialog key is synthesised on the human's behalf.

Run diagnostics of the new start step (trust flag or trust write, and any failure of it) never reach the terminal; they go to the log as codes only, carrying no path, no config content and no project entry.
Any new error of the trust write is a codes-only error: its message interpolates nothing, it carries no path, and no stack trace or bare status stands as its text.

If the start path gains a refusal for an absent, unreadable, linked or non-JSON config (a bound left to the founder), it follows the start-refusal shape of viola run and revive start: unable line with a reason code beside it, one hint per code, the --json refusal document clean, its exit code fixed, and its fixed strings pinned by literal from design copy.
viola verify's step lines and its modal start killed with no key stay as they are unless P3 measures the mechanism must reach them; verify never types a byte into the trust dialog.
The fake agent's new trust-dialog screen is detected by its signature only; no check parses claude's screen content beyond signatures, and the boundary check never inspects claude content.

The e2e acceptance for v2-33 asserts at the TUI boundary only: no trust dialog shown, the input box reached, zero viola bytes typed, and another folder's trust entry unchanged — each predicate one that can fail when the mechanism is gone.
Time bounds of the new start step and of its waiting tests fall on the driver only, never on the human; a waiting test stays under the 20 s lint with a named timeout.
Live readings on the standing rig (starts by shape, count per CLI version, every byte the rig types) are recorded but never gate the build.
The relied claude trust behaviour is a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe; a failed probe reports as a verify step line with its code word, no colour carrying its meaning alone.
Output of plain modes stays free of SGR and C0/C1 control characters: any new line viola prints at a start (refusal, hint, verify step) is escaped and carries no colour off a terminal.

body_fields.convention: each new a11y assertion runs inside the existing test suites, not a separate a11y suite or driver
each new test is deterministic — zero flakiness, no retries, no skips in the CI test gate; a breach fails the build
each new boundary test is sequenced on records rather than on screen timing, and asserts zero viola bytes on the terminal
each new a11y failure surfaces as an ordinary nextest failure in the GitHub Actions push/PR workflow, with no a11y artifact of its own

body: The viola list board rows — its caption, order, colour, stale-row dim, NAME bold and truncation, and the unwrapped separator: the chunk adds nothing to the board.
viola --help rows (usage line, group labels, handoff row, served verbs): the chunk adds no verb and no flag to viola's own CLI.
viola link and unlink, plugin install, revive --list, and their exit 20/21 and result-line contracts: the chunk does not touch those verbs.
viola send, answer and wait contracts, the MCP wait tool's timeout and the MCP frame tools: the chunk changes no send, dialog-answer or wait behaviour.
Screen-reader targets and the manual Orca and keyboard passes: they are supplemental, gate nothing, and the chunk adds no output a reader would meet.
Absences of a web or graphical frontend, a touch surface, internationalization, and a rendered page with browser tooling: none is reached.
The structured violation JSON rows: the chunk adds no a11y report format.

**2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows** — made R8 a `CLAUDE*` prefix strip with the 11-name identity floor and `config.json` `claude_env_keep`, and set the child's cwd explicitly to viola's current directory (decision/child-cwd-explicit, decision/r8-identity-floor, decision/child-env-claude-strip). Matters here: a user's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is stripped from the child unless kept, so the trust write (or flag) must target the config file the child actually reads, and the folder to trust is exactly the explicit child cwd.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** (the R8 strip: exact names, `claude_env_keep` the one pass-list) — dropped the Windows registry reader; every inherited `CLAUDE*` name matched exactly is stripped except one named in `claude_env_keep`, the strip reading names only, never a value (decision/env-strip-names-only, decision/claude-env-stripped-from-child). Matters here: resolving `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to locate the CLI's config would read a value the strip never reads — a widening to name, and the rig's private `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` must still reach its child.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** (the identity floor's Linux reading) — measured the `CLAUDE*` names a hook and a session are handed on Linux, kept the floor at eleven (decision/identity-floor-eleven-names) and registered `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` etc. as names viola reads none of (decision/plugin-env-vars-unused). Matters here: the environment the wrapped child sees is a measured, ruled set; any trust mechanism through an env key must fit the strip and the floor.

**2026-09-27-instance-state-and-start-order** — landed the start order (resolution → collision → pin + plugin → version gate → bind → snapshot + heartbeat → events → spawn) and the one shared tempfile `persist` helper `viola_state::fs::replace_private` with mode set before any byte (decision/run-start-order, decision/atomic-replaced-state-files, decision/private-mode-before-write). Matters here: a trust write before the spawn needs its own place in the start order, and any file viola writes goes through the shared helpers, never its own temp + rename.

**2026-10-27-pinned-copy-race-and-reproducible-builds** ([Snapshot writer]: the pinned copy's no-clobber placement) — added `place_private_new` (`persist_noclobber`) beside the replace helpers after a measured concurrent-start race (decision/tempfile-snapshot-writer). Matters here: `~/.claude.json` is rewritten by the host's own Claude sessions about once a minute, so a read-edit-replace races them — the precedent for measuring a write race and choosing the helper by its race behaviour, not assuming it.

**2026-11-05-linux-only-code-and-ci** ([Snapshot writer]: `replace_private` is one attempt) — retired the retry loop; a failed `persist` returns at once with the target as it was. Matters here: a replace of the CLI's state file gets one attempt and no retry, and leaves the file untouched on failure — the write form must still lose no other session's write.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** (screen signatures compiled, ten ledger rows, verify's interactive runs) — compiled the modal literal `Yes, I trust this folder` (and `Yes, allow external imports`); verify's Run A runs untrusted in an OS-temp dir and is killed with no key, Run B trusted in `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>/`; measured on 2.1.288 that trust is inherited from a trusted parent while the external-imports approval is keyed on the git root (decision/screen-signatures-compiled, decision/verify-types-nothing-into-dialogs, decision/no-typing-into-trust-dialogs). Matters here: the trust modal is a gate-refusing modal, verify relies on an untrusted Run A raising it, and parent-inheritance changes which folder a trust record must name.

**2026-10-05-real-cli-verify-probes** (registry rows for verify's interactive runs) — the fake agent gained `--trusted-root` / `--screens` (argv, no env); the two probe dirs and the never-a-key-into-a-CLI-dialog rule are the founder's live rulings. Matters here: the fake agent must raise its trust dialog in an untrusted folder and honour the chosen mechanism, extending `--trusted-root`'s precedent; a fake-agent screen change puts `cli_verify` in the gate.

**2026-10-05-dialog-rows-and-re-probe** — verify's Runs C and D pass `--settings <DIALOG_SETTINGS>` and a 0700 `plans/` inside their own dirs, a founder-ratified widening of the verify child set. Matters here: precedent that a verify run's extra CLI flag or settings is a named widening; if the chosen trust mechanism must reach verify's runs, it widens that ratified child set (decision/verify-child-set).

**2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows** (Run B's probe --settings, the statusline capture arm) — Run B got one probe `--settings` file, ratified by the founder as a boundary widening of the verify child set. Matters here: the precedent for a CLI flag added to a verify run under ratification, and for where the agent crate holds a flag literal verify reads.

**2026-10-13-paste-newline-ledger-row** — added the 18th ledger row; a stamp of the older id set reads unverified, so every home stamped before reads `cli_verified:false` until its next `viola verify` (decision/version-verified-all-relied-rows). Matters here: a new trust ledger row with its verify probe (the scope's expectation) unverifies every stamped home and needs a live re-stamp, counted against the founder's live cap.

**2026-10-14-resume-and-compact-ledger-rows** — added Run E in a guarded `<cwd>/.viola-verify-<pid>-resume/` with the 22nd row, a founder-ratified widening of verify's child set (decision/verify-child-set, decision/verify-run-e-resumes-run-b-first-session). Matters here: a new probe run for a trust row follows this pattern (own private dir, drop guard, ratified widening, live re-stamp).

**2026-11-16-local-command-delivery** — added the `local-command-echo-probe` ledger row with its own verify probe, and send reads the CLI's session transcript to confirm (decision/local-command-echo-probe). Matters here: the latest precedent for a relied CLI behaviour landing as a ledger row plus a verify probe, and for viola reading a CLI-owned file under a ratified decision.

**2026-11-15-api-error-turn-end** — StopFailure registered with no ledger row and no verify probe, a named exception to decision/capability-ledger, decision/cli-capability-ledger and decision/capability-ledger-gate (ratified at 2026-11-16T06-05-33-wrap). Matters here: the only precedent for a relied CLI behaviour without a row; a trust flag or record taken without a row would need the same explicit founder exception.

**2026-10-07-live-rows-and-paste-shapes-on-the-dev-host** (the long-paste frame) — the founder ruled the limit «a shape no send relies on needs no probe» (decision/no-probe-for-unrelied-shapes, the capability-ledger-gate except). Matters here: a trust mechanism every start relies on is not such a shape, so the ruled limit does not excuse it from a row.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** — viola wrote a per-session code-bearing settings override at every start, through `replace_private` after the first snapshot and before the spawn, handed to the child with `--settings`, and read the user's `.claude/settings.json` as a source. Matters here: the nearest precedent for viola writing a CLI-consumed config before the spawn and reading the user's Claude config — and how such a write was placed in the start order.

**2026-10-10-statusline-pass-through** (four crossings ratified by the founder) — the override, the shell-out and the user-settings read were each shown to the founder as a boundary widening and ratified; set the standing rule «Boundary widening the founder already answered» (still one card at the wrap). Matters here: writing `~/.claude.json` is named a widening by the scope and follows this procedure, its bound the founder's.

**2026-11-14-status-line-interception-removed** — retired the settings override and the statusline source read whole: absence/status-line-interception (no settings layer, no `--settings` at start, no statusLine source read); `--settings` now only a literal verify reads (decision/claude-flag-literals-in-agent-crate); child argv is `--plugin-dir` then the caller's args. Matters here: the scope's «no `--settings`, no settings.json override» boundary rests on this absence; a trust flag joins the child argv contract and its literal belongs in the agent crate.

**2026-09-28-capability-ledger-and-viola-verify** (the version gate placed and split by crate) — Claude parsing and rows live in the pure `viola-agent-claude` with no `viola-state` dependency; file I/O in `viola_state` and the root bin (decision/agent-claude-pure, decision/claude-first-no-adapter-trait). Matters here: the trust key names or flag literal go in the agent crate, while any write of the CLI's config lives outside it.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (the snapshot's `cwd` and the child's second cwd source) — a revived start spawns in the snapshot's recorded `cwd`, read after the strict-modes check and required to exist (else `cwd-missing`), ratified as a boundary widening (decision/child-cwd-explicit except, contract/instance-snapshot/cwd). Matters here: whether revive's start arm trusts its recorded directory — a different folder than viola's cwd.

**2026-10-10-viola-revive** (revive as the second way a wrapper starts) — a passing revive goes through the same start as `run` and resumes in place (decision/revive-in-place, decision/revive-resumes-in-place). Matters here: a trust step placed in the shared start reaches revive too, so the scope's open question on revive's arm is decided by where the step sits.

**2026-10-26-home-and-code-bearing-file-integrity** (the home-tree check before the start's and verify's log; the pin key taken once) — every start runs `check_home_tree` before its wrapper log opens, and pins the very bytes its check hashed (decision/strict-check-before-log-open, decision/strict-modes-check-before-log, decision/run-pins-checked-bytes). Matters here: a new start step must sit after these checks, and its refusal (if any) writes no line before the log.

**2026-10-27-bounded-inputs-at-every-boundary** — every product reader of external bytes is bounded in its statement or named in `tests/contract_bounded_readers.rs`'s `EXCEPTIONS`; serde_json's `unbounded_depth` banned (decision/bounded-readers, decision/no-unbounded-json-depth). Matters here: reading `~/.claude.json` is a new external reader that must land bounded with its `BOUNDARIES` row and witness, or the census goes red — note the host file may be large.

**2026-10-31-sanitised-error-surfaces** — CLI `--json` documents, MCP results and channel errors carry codes and fixed messages only, no path or upstream text; `thiserror` messages interpolate nothing (decision/sanitised-error-surfaces, decision/thiserror-messages-interpolate-nothing). Matters here: a failure reading or writing the CLI's config must surface as a closed code with no path or content, matching the scope's «nothing of the CLI's config file logged».

**2026-10-31-exit-cause-code-catalogue** (`viola revive --json` documents every refusal of its start) — the start's refusals print a closed-code exit-1 document under `revive --json`, each code a row of `tests/contract_error_bodies.rs` and `tests/cross_exit_causes.rs` (contract/cli-json-error-document/shape, contract/cli-json-output/revive-refusal-codes). Matters here: a new start refusal (an unreadable or non-JSON config, if refused rather than fail-open) extends the closed code list, both tables and the hint census.

**2026-11-01-unix-endpoint-and-home-hardening** (the start's refused socket directory, exit 1) — added `socket-dir-refused` as a start refusal before any snapshot, child or bind, a founder-ratified widening (decision/socket-dir-refused-covers-create-and-check, contract/run-start-refusals/socket-dir-refused). Matters here: the latest precedent for inserting a checked step with its own closed code into the start order before the spawn.

**2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline** — `NO_COLOR`/`TERM`/`COLORTERM` reads ratified as a boundary widening, with the standing precedent that any further environment read needs its own ratification (decision/no-environment-configuration). Matters here: reading `HOME` or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to locate the CLI's config file is such a further environment read.

**2026-10-16-unwrapped-sessions-on-the-board** (the fake agent's agents mode) — the founder ruled files beside the fake agent's executable over a third fake-agent env seam. Matters here: honouring a trust mechanism in the fake agent should follow that precedent (argv or files, no new env seam; decision/env-var-viola-prefix's seams are ratified exceptions).

**2026-10-19-newer-claude-cli-rows** (the 2.1.302 fixture set and the long-turn screen switch) — the fake agent's option list is the count's rule (thirteen then) and the recorded screen sets are per CLI version. Matters here: a fake-agent trust-dialog mode or option moves that registered count and may need recorded screens for the stamped versions.

viola types into no trust dialog, in run, revive or verify; verify's runs stay as they are, never answering a CLI dialog and killing a modal start with no key, unless the measurement says the mechanism must reach them.

Where the mechanism sits in the start order: before the child spawn, the child spawned last, its cwd set explicitly; whether revive's start arm, resuming in place on the snapshot's recorded cwd, shares it.
If a flag arm is chosen: the flag is a new item of the flags passed to the claude child, its literal living only in the agent crate beside the other claude flag literals.
A flag or setting that does more than trust (one that skips permission prompts) is a widening of its own and is not taken without the founder's word.

If the record arm is chosen: the write to the CLI's state file lives outside viola-agent-claude, which does no file I/O, through viola-state's private-file discipline or a seam of its own; the agent crate holds only the key names.

The write's form against concurrent writers: the host's own claude sessions rewrite the config file about once a minute, so the write must lose no other session's write and none of viola's (crash-safe and atomic replace rules weighed against a file viola does not own).

The write's bound: only the trust key, only the session's own cwd entry, never another project's entry written or removed, and the handling of an absent, unreadable, linked or not-JSON config file — the bound being the founder's, not settled by the plan.

The relied CLI behaviour (the trust flag or the trust record honoured) is a version-stamped capability ledger row with a viola verify probe; a CLI version is verified only when every relied row passes, and real CLI probes run only locally.
Nothing of the CLI's config file is logged or surfaced: codes-only process logs, error chains only in the detail file, sanitised error surfaces and thiserror messages that interpolate nothing.
No settings layer: no --settings at start and no settings.json override written; the user's global statusline and settings stay untouched.

The fake agent raises its trust dialog in an untrusted folder and honours the chosen mechanism, so the e2e acceptance fails when the mechanism is gone; a change to its screens puts cli_verify in the gate block, and screen signatures stay compiled literals.

The standing rig's own trust pass into its private config must not mask the product's mechanism in the live starts that prove v2-33; the live starts are counted by shape and CLI version with every byte the rig types recorded.
Errors of the new step follow the crate error rules: thiserror per crate, anyhow only at the root bin edge, external config parsed tolerantly with unparseable values read as unknown.

body: The viola run start path gains a trust step before the claude child spawns, by the CLI's flag or setting or by a trust-record write for the session's cwd; the revive start arm shares it if P3 finds it shares the path, and revive start logs as run.

Nothing of the CLI's config file reaches any log line, span field, detail code or stderr line: not its path, not its contents, not the cwd's project key; the NEVER-log floor and codes-only errors hold for the new step.

A failure of the trust step (config file absent, unreadable, a link, not JSON, or a lost write) surfaces only as a closed code word with no path or pid, on the run start's process-exit line or as a parse-rejected detail for the config file's parser; whether it refuses the start or falls through is the founder's bound.

The trust step's read-edit-write against the host's own sessions rewriting the config file about once a minute must lose no other writer's write, and may not be made safe by a retry loop: retry policies are forbidden.

If the flag arm is chosen, the flag joins the claude child's argv: the child's settings argument and env values are never logged, the run start span attributes carry no path, endpoint or env value, and the claude-child process-start line keeps env names and counts only.

The R8 CLAUDE strip decides which config file the child reads: a user's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR may not reach the child, and the stripped CLAUDE values stay unlogged even where the trust step must target the file the child actually reads.

viola types no key into the CLI-native trust dialog and logs no typed key, no PTY byte and no dialog text; the viola verify runs stay as they are (no byte into the trust dialog, a modal start killed with no key) unless P3 measures that the mechanism must reach them.

The relied trust behaviour of the undocumented claude CLI becomes a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe: verify lines carry no content, ledger contents are never logged, an unreadable ledger means an unverified CLI, and the real-CLI verify never runs in CI.

The fake agent raises a trust dialog in an untrusted folder and honours the chosen mechanism; a change to its screens puts cli_verify in the gate block, and CI verify runs against the fake agent only.

The v2-33 e2e acceptance can fail: with the mechanism removed the fake agent's dialog rises and the test fails; it also checks the user's trust of another folder is unchanged; its waits stay under the 20 s kill line.

Live starts on the standing rig prove v2-33 by shape and count per CLI version with every byte the rig types listed; the rig's own trust pass must not mask the product's, its private CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR must still reach its child, and every started process ends.
viola run stays silent on the terminal: the trust step adds no terminal output beyond the existing start-refusal unable and hint pair, and the refusal message is fixed and pathless.

A trust write through the state crate's private-file discipline observes its file operations at viola's call site with synchronous instrumentation, and a refused link or strict-modes failure writes the refusal's code only, never the skipped path.
The trust step adds no product event to the events log and keeps the run start events' order; any new span sits inside the run.start chain under a static name.

Wrapped claude internals and its config file layout are not a contract: the trust-record key names live only in viola-agent-claude, and any recorded fixture of the CLI's screens or config is scrub-required.

body: The rule that viola writes nothing under the Claude home or in Claude's config: the record arm, if chosen, is a named widening of it, amended by a Decisions Log entry whose bound (which key, which cwd, when, never another project's entry, absent, unreadable, link or not-JSON file, nothing logged) is the founder's.

No settings override and no settings file written to the child: the trust mechanism may not be a settings injection.

Never a key typed into the trust dialog by viola: verify never answers or types into a dialog, and the live rig keys only into its own pty, its dialog and box keys counted apart from the standing stop.

The R8 CLAUDE environment strip and the parent identity variables stripped from the child: the trust flag or write must target the config file the child actually reads, and the rig's private CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR must still reach its child; any new environment read takes its log entry.

CLAUDE values and the Claude config file's content are never logged: the never-log floor and codes-only, non-interpolating error messages hold for every failure of the trust step, with no path in external error output.

Reading the Claude config file is a new external reader: it is bounded or named in the readers census, parsed tolerantly with the default JSON depth limit, and an absent, unreadable, linked or non-JSON file is handled by the founder's bound.

A write to the Claude config file must lose no concurrent session's write nor viola's own, through one shared replace helper or a seam of its own, with the file's mode kept; the phase says plainly if it cannot.
The recorded cwd is the folder trusted: the spawn directory kept in the snapshot only, revive spawning in the recorded cwd, and only that cwd's entry touched.

Every dependence on an undocumented claude behaviour is a capability-ledger row with a viola verify probe; the trust flag literal or record key names stay compiled literals in the Claude adapter, which does no file I/O.

viola verify's runs stay as they are, needing a pre-trusted folder and killing a modal start with no key, unless the measurement shows the mechanism must reach them; its probe effects stay confined to its own directory.

The live standing rig's child stays isolated from the user's config and its credentials copy transient; the rig's own trust pass must not mask the product's mechanism in the live starts proving v2-33, and the effect of viola's write on the founder's real config during a live start is reported.
Configuration, an environment variable or a flag never switches off a control: the trust step adds no switch that disables a security check.
claude is resolved from the caller's PATH and the child trusts PATH; the measurement reads the installed CLI's help and bundle strings as content, never as commands.
The run start order holds: the home tree and socket directory checks come before the trust step and the child spawn, and a refusal leaves no trace in the Claude config file.
